title: Localized coefficient square and its derived comparison identity
statement: Let f:X to Y be a morphism of schemes, R and S coefficient ring sheaves with an identified inverse image, F the exact complex pullback, L its derived functor, epsilon its specified factors, and a,b any specified tensor models. Let P,H,M be arbitrary cochain complexes, P,H and FP,FH flat-term K-flat, and q:H to M any map. Let eY and eX be isomorphisms between the localized total tensors for (P,H),(P,M) and (FP,FH),(FP,FM), whose forward maps are Q(1 tensor q) and Q(1 tensor Fq). Then epsilon at Tot(P,M), followed by Q(sigma(P,M)) and eX inverse followed by the b representative comparison and tensor(1,QFq), equals L of eY inverse followed by the a representative comparison and tensor(1,Qq), then tau(QP,QM), then tensor(epsilonP,epsilonM). Dependencies: the pro-etale operations, signed total tensor and canonical representative comparisons in the statement dependencies below.

proof.text: Localize the chain comparison square, and rewrite its two vertical maps with the prescribed forward maps of eY,eX. Naturality of epsilon at 1 tensor q relates the left vertical map to L(eY.hom).

Precompose the final asserted identity by the invertible L(Q(u)). Naturality of epsilon at u and the localized chain square turn its left side into epsilon_T Q(sigma_PH) r_X tensor(1,QFq), cancelling Q(v) with eX inverse. Substitute the top representative square. Naturality of epsilon at q and bifunctoriality combine tensor(epsilon_P,epsilon_H) with tensor(1,QFq) into tensor(1,LQq) followed by tensor(epsilon_P,epsilon_M). Naturality of tau moves the first factor across tau. Finally functoriality of L and cancellation of Q(u) with eY inverse give the right side. No step requires flatness of N or K-flatness of Tot(P tensor N[0]).
